</tr>
<tr>

<td><b>3. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wAJURzAaGLQ">Creating a Codespace on Main And Asking Agent for Issue</a></b><br>Starts a codespace on main, logs in to Claude Code, and asks for assigned issues. </tr>

<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8xySDxowoE"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/E8xySDxowoE/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Making the Issue Branch, Creating the Plan, Fixing the Bug"></a></td>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>

## PRISM Product Graph Editor (Oct 26)

<table class="playlist">
<tr>
<td width="320"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSglZScsi7LA"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/DmLMN0XQrkU/hqdefault.jpg" width="320" alt="PRISM Product Graph Editor playlist"></a></td>
<td><b><a href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSglZScsi7LA">Playlist: PRISM Product Graph Editor</a></b> · 8 videos<br>An eight-part tour of the Product Graph Editor, PRISM's main web app. It covers where the app and engine live, the graph editor and its YAML files, then each results tab: inventory, impact analysis, process results, contribution tree and Sankey graphs, using the cotton fiber and jacket templates.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmLMN0XQrkU"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/DmLMN0XQrkU/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Introduction to Product Graph Editor"></a></td>
<td><b>1. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmLMN0XQrkU">Introduction to Product Graph Editor</a></b><br>Where things live in the prism-lca org. The engine, life-cycle-assessment-mcp, is built on Brightway, runs on DigitalOcean, and has a REST API for the web app and an MCP for LLMs. The editor is JavaScript on GitHub Pages and rebuilds whenever main changes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VImCZZTk-sI"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/VImCZZTk-sI/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="The Graph Editor - Structure Graph, Scaled Graph"></a></td>
<td><b>2. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VImCZZTk-sI">The Graph Editor - Structure Graph, Scaled Graph</a></b><br>Sign in with Google, pick a template, and explore the cotton fiber and jacket graphs. The structure graph shows how activities connect; the scaled graph shows the amounts needed for the functional unit. Also covers reference amounts, elementary and technosphere flows, and graph controls.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oOE0noTj0hM"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/oOE0noTj0hM/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Product Graph Yaml Files"></a></td>
<td><b>3. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oOE0noTj0hM">Product Graph Yaml Files</a></b><br>The Edit tab shows the model as a readable YAML file with the goal, functional unit, products, and each process's inputs, outputs and emissions. The File menu loads templates, saves, downloads and uploads YAML files, shows edit history, and clears the session.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1MQ_rXXDIZ4"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/1MQ_rXXDIZ4/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Inventory Results"></a></td>
<td><b>4. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1MQ_rXXDIZ4">Inventory Results</a></b><br>Using the jacket graph, covers the global settings for decimal places and light or dark mode, then the LCA results summary: life cycle inventory totals and five TRACI impact scores. The Inventory tab lists total emissions and how much each process produces.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q3j6pYukn-I"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/q3j6pYukn-I/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Impact Analysis"></a></td>
<td><b>5. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q3j6pYukn-I">Impact Analysis</a></b><br>The Impact Analysis tab breaks each impact category down by processes then flows, or flows then processes. Characterization factors show how scores are calculated: for climate change, each kilogram of methane counts 25 times as much as CO2, and everything is summed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fbP868qBino"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/fbP868qBino/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Process Results"></a></td>
<td><b>6. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fbP868qBino">Process Results</a></b><br>Process Results looks at one activity at a time. The top shows its inputs and outputs; the bottom shows its share of each impact score, split into upstream and direct. For example, fabric weaving contributes 75% of climate change and 54% of acidification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BB8ZiB5HYng"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/BB8ZiB5HYng/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Contribution Tree Analysis"></a></td>
<td><b>7. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BB8ZiB5HYng">Contribution Tree Analysis</a></b><br>The contribution tree drills down from the functional unit to find hotspots. For the jacket's climate change score, fabric weaving gives 75%, zipper production 8% and jacket assembly itself about 16%. Each row shows direct and accumulated contributions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="240"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OUnZ5Y5gk8A"><img src="https://img.youtube.com/vi/OUnZ5Y5gk8A/mqdefault.jpg" width="240" alt="Sankey Graphs"></a></td>
<td><b>8. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OUnZ5Y5gk8A">Sankey Graphs</a></b><br>The Sankey tab shows contributions as line thickness, by impact category or by flow, with filters for the number of processes and minimum share. Each card shows direct and upstream amounts, and clicking an activity highlights everything feeding into it.</td>
</tr>
</table>
